authTierRationale: Only one credential mode is offered. The user must (1) register their own private JWT Auth app in the RingCentral Developer Console to obtain client_id + client_secret (T2), and (2) additionally generate a long-lived JWT credential in the console and authorize it for that app. The JWT is a long-lived assertion the connector repeatedly exchanges for short-lived bearer access tokens via the urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer grant — functionally the same user burden as supplying a refresh token, hence T3. The README states explicitly that Estuary does not host an OAuth app (RingCentral charges per registered app) and that a hosted flow is only a future plan; spec() returns oauth2=None, so there is no control-plane-assisted path today.

unionMisfits.description: The response envelope carries `navigation.nextPage.uri` (a full next-page URL), but the connector never follows or parses that URL — it uses only its PRESENCE as a has-more boolean and independently increments its own `page` query parameter. This is neither `next_url` (URL not followed) nor a pure `terminateOn: envelope_flag` (the field is a URL object, not a flag), so it is recorded as type `page` with terminateOn `absent_token`. A more faithful shape would let a page paginator name the envelope field whose absence terminates it.

RFC 7523 jwt-bearer is not one of the `grant` enum values. The exchange POSTs form fields grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer plus assertion=<user JWT>, authenticated with HTTP Basic (base64 client_id:client_secret) on the token endpoint; the resulting access_token is then sent to the API as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. That is three schemes composed (basic on the token endpoint, jwt-bearer grant, bearer on the API) which the flat union cannot express — `grant: refresh_token` was chosen as the nearest fit because the JWT plays the role of a user-supplied long-lived refresh credential.

proposedShape.scopesFrom: space-delimited `scope` string in the token response

unionMisfits.description: Every request is bounded on BOTH sides — dateFrom (cursor) and dateTo (now, or the startup cutoff for backfill) — but `incrementalParam` models only the lower bound. The upper bound is load-bearing here: backfill uses it to define its cutoff and the incremental leg uses it to advance the cursor when no records are returned.

The call-log API filters by startTime, not lastModifiedTime, so the connector cannot query 'modified since'. It tracks max startTime as the cursor and, once per day (when the cursor crosses a date boundary), rewinds dateFrom by `lookback_window` hours to re-fetch and re-emit updated records, deduplicating via the CDK emitted_changes_cache keyed on lastModifiedTime. The schema has no place to record a cursor-rewind/lookback policy.

cursorRewind.trigger: cursor date differs from today's date

unionMisfits.description: Rate limiting is a first-class, hand-rolled part of this connector (per-API-group 60-second sliding windows: heavy=10/min for call logs, medium=40/min for extensions and internal contacts, light=50/min for messages and external contacts) because RingCentral imposes a 60-second penalty on any 429. The transport spec has nowhere to record per-endpoint rate classes, yet they materially bound throughput.

abstained.transports[0].spec.baseUrl (sandbox host: The base URL is a hard-coded constant pointing at the PRODUCTION host platform.ringcentral.com. There is no environment/sandbox toggle anywhere in constants.py, models.py's EndpointConfig, or the spec snapshot, so no sandbox host is recorded. RingCentral's sandbox host is not named anywhere in the connector source; inferring it would be a guess.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No static headers are set by the connector; only the CDK-injected Authorization header. Nothing further is asserted.
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.pathPlaceholders (real: Both {accountId} and {extensionId} are the literal self-reference `~` in every ENDPOINT constant; the connector never resolves them to numeric ids and exposes no config field for them. The concrete account/extension is therefore whatever the JWT credential authenticates as, which the source does not name.
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.paginator.pageSize (re: PAGE_SIZE=100 is what the connector sends; the README notes the API's per-endpoint maximum varies between 100 and 250, but no per-endpoint maxima are encoded in the source.
abstained.streams[3].writeDisposition: Recorded as merge because the key is /id and the lookback re-emits updated call-log records for the same id, but no explicit reduction/merge annotation appears in the connector — this follows from CDK defaults for keyed incremental bindings rather than an explicit statement in this connector.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.scopes (ReadAc: Scope.READ_ACCOUNT_CALL_LOG is defined in constants.py but is not referenced by any resource's REQUIRED_SCOPES, so it is not listed among the scopes actually required. Whether it is dead code or intended for a future account-wide call-log stream is not determinable from the source.
abstained.execution.continuity: mode is poll over a stateless REST API; no server-side artifacts (slots, consumer groups, scratch tables) are created and nothing accrues on the customer side between ticks. The only pause-related risk is RingCentral's own data retention, which is not encoded in the connector.
